H8610.d: to manipulate, i.e. seize; chiefly to capture, wield, specifically, to overlay; figuratively, to use unwarrantably

H8659.d: Tarshish, a place on the Mediterranean, hence, the ephithet of a merchant vessel (as if for or from that port); also the name of a Persian and of an Israelite
fb: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Tarshish. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.
Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.

H8646.d: Terach, the father of Abraham; also a place in the Desert
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Abraham's father, whose family line Genesis 11 traces. Joshua 24:2 names him again.
Named twice, in Numbers, and nowhere else.

H8655.d: Teraphim (singular or plural) a family idol

H8628.d: to clatter, i.e. slap (the hands together), clang (an instrument); by analogy, to drive (a nail or tent-pin, a dart, etc.); by implication, to become bondsman by handclasping)

H8641.d: a present (as offered up), especially in sacrifice or as tribute

H8622.d: a revolution, i.e. (of the sun) course, (of time) lapse

H8643.d: clamor, i.e. acclamation of joy or a battle-cry; especially clangor of trumpets, as an alarum

H8636.d: multiplication, i.e. percentage or bonus in addition to principal

H8656.d: Tirtsah, a place in Palestine; also an Israelitess
fb: An old Canaanite royal city that served as capital of the northern kingdom before Samaria was built. The Song of Solomon sets its beauty beside Jerusalem's. Menahem seized the throne from there.
Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
She was the youngest of Zelophehad's five daughters, named with her sisters each time the family's inheritance comes up.

H8603.d: Tophel, a place near the Desert
fb: Deuteronomy opens with Moses speaking to Israel near Tophel. It is generally identified with Tafileh, on the edge of the Edomite plateau east of the Dead Sea.

H8615.d: literally a cord (as an attachment); figuratively, expectancy

fb: A town given to Benjamin, in the hill country near Gibeon. Nobody has found the site.

H8668.d: rescue (literal or figurative, persons, national or spiritual)

H8666.d: a recurrence (of time or place); a reply (as returned)

H8605.d: intercession, supplication; by implication, a hymn

fb: It sat about six miles south of Bethlehem, on the edge of the wilderness that carries its name. Rehoboam fortified it, and Amos was a herdsman there when he was called to prophesy against Israel.

H8621.d: a Tekoite or inhabitant of Tekoah
fb: Someone from Tekoa, the hometown of Amos. The wise woman Joab sent to David about Absalom was a Tekoite, and so were at least two of David's mighty men.
Solomon's rule reached as far as Tipsah, a crossing on the Euphrates the Greeks called Thapsacus. Menahem sacked it when he seized Israel's throne because it would not open its gates to him.
Menahem took this town and treated it savagely. The other Tipsah is the Euphrates crossing at the far edge of Solomon's reach.

H8664.d: a Tishbite or inhabitant of Tishbeh (in Gilead)
fb: Elijah is always the Tishbite, the man from Tishbe. Where Tishbe was, in Gilead or further north in Galilee, depends on how you read the Hebrew of 1 Kings 17:1.

H8662.d: Tartak, a deity of the Avvites
fb: A male deity in the Old Testament
One of two gods the Avvites worshipped after the Assyrians resettled them in Samaria. The other was Nibhaz, and nothing else is known about this one.
An Assyrian title, roughly commander-in-chief, not a man's name. One tartan came with the delegation demanding Jerusalem's surrender from Hezekiah, and an earlier one took Ashdod for Sargon.
King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

The Kushite pharaoh of Egypt in the early seventh century BC, known in his own records as Taharqa. Word that he was marching against Assyria made Sennacherib send Hezekiah a threatening letter during the siege of Jerusalem.

H8616.d: Tikvah, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
His son Shallum was married to Huldah, the prophetess who was asked about the law scroll found in Josiah's temple repairs.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Father of one of the men who stood against the foreign-marriage decision under Ezra.
The place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned to Molech, until Josiah defiled it. Jeremiah said the valley would fill with the dead. Later Jewish pictures of Gehenna drew on it.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Caleb's son by his concubine Maachah, in Judah's genealogy, and that is all.

H8654.d: a Tirathite or inhabitant of an unknown Tirah
fb: Scribal group in the Old Testament
Scribes at Jabez, named with the Shimeathites and Suchathites. They were Kenites from Hammath, father of the house of Rechab.

H8660.d: the title of a Persian deputy or governor
fb: A Persian word for the governor of Judah, not a name. It is used of Nehemiah, and on one reading of Zerubbabel.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He was a Persian governor who challenged the Jews rebuilding the temple and wrote to Darius about it. The search turned up Cyrus's decree, and he was told to help instead.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return

He and Bigthan guarded the door of King Ahasuerus and plotted to kill him. Mordecai found out and reported it, and both men were executed. The record of that service was later read to the king, and it turned the story of Esther.

H8608.d: to drum, i.e. play (as) on the tambourine

H8626.d: to equalize, i.e. straighten (intransitive or transitive); figuratively, to compose

H8650.d: a pole (as a mast or flagstaff)

fb: The place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned to Molech, until Josiah defiled it. Jeremiah said the valley would fill with the dead. Later Jewish pictures of Gehenna drew on it.

H8645.d: a species of tree (apparently from its slenderness), perhaps the cypress

H8651.d: a door; by implication, a palace

H8631.d: to become (causatively, make) mighty or (figuratively) obstinate
